title: Same 50 stocks, opposite results
intro: Two indices with identical constituents — one lost money over the year, the other gained 8%. The whole difference is weights.

steps.title: The clean experiment
steps.body:
The **Nifty 50** and the **Nifty 50 Equal Weight**: same 50 companies, same reconstitution schedule, same universe. Over the past year (to July 24, 2026): **Nifty 50 −2.3%, Equal Weight +8.2%**. Over three years: **6.7% vs 14.0% a year**.

Not a single stock tells them apart. Only *how much of each*.

steps.title: Where the weight sits
steps.body: In the Nifty 50, the **top 10 stocks are more than half** the index; the bottom 10 contribute **under 7%**. In the Equal Weight index, every group of ten is roughly a fifth.

points.label: N50 top 10
points.note: Over half the index — the heavyweights ARE the index. When they stall, the index stalls regardless of the other 40.

points.label: N50 bottom 10
points.note: Under 7% combined — forty stocks that barely matter to the number you see.

points.label: EW any 10
points.note: Each group of ten ≈ one-fifth: the index actually owns its breadth.

steps.title: A judgement, not a neutral fact
steps.body:
> [!key] Every index carries **a judgement about what deserves weight**. Market cap rewards whatever grew — whether fundamentals or fashion drove it. A passive *factor* index makes the judgement explicit; a market-cap index just hides it better.

This past year the heavyweights lagged and the other forty worked — so equal weight won. When the heavyweights do the work, the same arithmetic reverses.

steps.title: The portfolio echo
steps.body: The same lesson one level up: your **portfolio's** result is set by its weights, not its holdings list. Five funds sharing the same top-ten is one concentrated bet in five wrappers — which is exactly why 'genuine diversification underneath the surface' is one of the yearly four checks.

recap:
**Weights, not names, set outcomes.**

- Same 50 stocks: −2.3% vs +8.2% in one year; 6.7 vs 14.0%/yr over three.
- N50: top 10 > half; bottom 10 < 7%. EW: every ten ≈ 20%.
- Market-cap weighting is a judgement — own it knowingly.
- Audit portfolios by weight and overlap, not fund count.
